{"id":"PKIX-str9","title":"pkix-path cannot parse pre-1970 UTCTime: PKITS 4.2.3 fails, diff-harness red on main since 2026-11-16","description":"## Observed

NIST PKITS "4.2.3 Valid pre2000 UTC notBefore Date Test3" fails to parse:

  malformed ASN.1 DER value for UTCTime at DER byte 114

The certificate is pkix-path/tests/pkits/certs/Validpre2000UTCnotBeforeDateTest3EE.crt. openssl reads it without complaint:

  notBefore=Jan  1 12:01:00 1950 GMT
  notAfter=Dec 31 08:30:00 2030 GMT

   99:d=3 hl=2 l=13 prim: UTCTIME :500101120100Z
  114:d=3 hl=2 l=13 prim: UTCTIME :301231083000Z

Reproduced locally straight through x509_cert::Certificate::from_der, so this is not a path-validation issue. The certificate never parses at all.

## Why this is a real bug, not a bad fixture

RFC 5280 section 4.1.2.5.1 defines UTCTime as spanning 1950-2049: "Where YY is greater than or equal to 50, the year SHALL be interpreted as 19YY; and where YY is less than 50, the year SHALL be interpreted as 20YY."

So notBefore=1950 is legal, and PKITS classes this chain as VALID -- the test exists precisely to check that a pre-2000 UTCTime is accepted. A library that cannot parse it rejects certificates RFC 5280 permits.

## Likely cause, to confirm before fixing

der's UtcTime is backed by a duration since the Unix epoch, which cannot represent a pre-1970 instant. That would explain rejecting 1950.

But note the reported offset: byte 114 is the notAfter field, an ordinary 2030 value that should decode without trouble. Byte 99 is the 1950 notBefore. So either the offset is misattributed, or the failure surfaces only when the Validity SEQUENCE completes. Pin that down first, because it decides whether the fix belongs in der, in a local UTCTime decode, or only in the error reporting.

Decode the two UTCTime values in isolation before touching anything.

## How this surfaced: a CI gate nobody was reading

.github/workflows/diff-harness.yml has been FAILING on main since at least 2026-11-16 -- three consecutive failures on main pushes. I did not know the workflow existed; it turned up in gh run list after today's push.

It compares the PKITS verdict-class summary against pkix-difftest/baseline-pkits.json and reports:

  -    "Agreement": 71,              +    "Agreement": 63,
  -    "DiagnosticDivergence": 49,   +    "DiagnosticDivergence": 58,

Eight chains moved from Agreement to DiagnosticDivergence against the committed baseline. Whether that drift is this parse bug, the oracle issue below, or an unrelated regression is NOT yet established -- do not assume.

Two harness errors per run:

1. pkix-path on "4.2.3 Valid pre2000 UTC notBefore Date Test3" -- this bug.
2. pyca on "4.1.5 Valid DSA Parameter Inheritance Test5" -- pyca's ASN.1 parser rejects an SPKI with inherited/absent DSA parameters. That is an oracle limitation rather than a pkix-path defect, and probably belongs as an expected skip instead of a harness error.

## Why P1

A parse failure on a certificate RFC 5280 allows is a correctness bug in the core crate, and pkix-path is published at 0.4.0 on crates.io, so this affects real consumers.

Separately, and worth stating plainly: a red CI gate on main that nobody reads is worse than no gate. It was the one signal that would have caught the eight-chain drift, and it had been red for over a week while work continued on top of it.

## Acceptance

[ ] Cause confirmed by decoding both UTCTime values in isolation, and the misattributed byte offset explained
[ ] Pre-1970 UTCTime parses; or the limitation is documented with its reason and PKITS 4.2.3 becomes an explicit expected-failure rather than a silent harness error
[ ] The eight-chain Agreement/DiagnosticDivergence drift explained -- fixed, or the baseline updated with the reason recorded
[ ] The pyca DSA-parameter-inheritance case classified as an oracle skip
[ ] diff-harness green on main","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T02:12:08.364569437Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T02:12:08.364569437Z"}

{"notes":"REVISED 2026-11-25 after Mark pushed back on the priority, the ownership and whether anyone cares. He was right on all three. Downgraded P1 -> P3.

## It is NOT our bug

der 0.8.3's UtcTime rejects pre-1970 values. Tested in isolation, decoding bare UTCTime TLVs with no certificate involved:

  500101120100Z (1950)  FAIL -- malformed ASN.1 DER value for UTCTime
  700101000000Z (1970)  OK
  301231083000Z (2030)  OK

pkix-path only propagates it. The fix is upstream in RustCrypto's der, or a documented limitation here -- not a change to our parsing.

## The byte-offset discrepancy is explained

The bead originally flagged that the error pointed at byte 114 (the 2030 notAfter) rather than byte 99 (the 1950 notBefore), and said to pin that down before fixing anything. Resolved: the offset is one past the END of the failing value. The 1950 UTCTime occupies bytes 99..114, so 114 is where the reader stopped. The isolated test reproduces this exactly -- a 15-byte TLV fails "at DER byte 15". It was the notBefore all along, consistently reported.

## Nobody cares about a cert dated 1951, and that was the right question

No CA issues certificates with pre-1970 dates. The only consumer of this code path is the NIST PKITS conformance corpus, which includes 4.2.3 precisely to exercise the boundary.

And the failure mode is FAIL-CLOSED: the certificate does not parse, so it is rejected. Rejecting a bizarre certificate is the safe direction. There is no security impact and no realistic deployment impact.

What remains is a conformance claim: the workspace ships PKITS as its test suite and fails a chain PKITS classes VALID. That is worth recording and worth fixing eventually. It is not worth P1.

## The 8-chain drift is BENIGN, which changes the whole picture

The original bead treated the Agreement 71 -> 63 / DiagnosticDivergence 49 -> 58 drift as possibly a real regression. It is not.

Class::DiagnosticDivergence means "everyone agrees on Pass/Fail but differs on the reason" -- rank 3 of 0-4, where 0 is worst and 4 is noise. So eight chains moved from "identical verdicts and identical diagnostics" to "identical verdicts, different diagnostic text". NO VERDICT CHANGED. pkix-path decided the same thing about all 121 chains.

The near-certain cause is an OpenSSL or pyca version bump on the GitHub runner changing error wording. The harness documents its own sensitivity to this: "The diff harness's verdicts are sensitive to the exact OpenSSL build (option string parsing, error wording) and pyca release."

## So the real problem is the gate, not the library

diff-harness compares diagnostic TEXT against a committed baseline while running against whatever OpenSSL and pyca the runner happens to ship. That makes it red on third-party version bumps that say nothing about pkix-path. It went red around 2026-11-16 and stayed red through at least three main pushes, which is exactly what a gate does when it cries wolf: it stops being read.

A gate nobody reads is worse than no gate. That is the thing to fix, and it is a different problem from the UTCTime limitation. Filed separately.

## Revised acceptance for THIS bead (P3)

[ ] Upstream issue filed against RustCrypto der for pre-1970 UtcTime, or a decision recorded that we will not pursue it
[ ] PKITS 4.2.3 classed as an explicit expected-failure with this reason, so it stops surfacing as an anonymous harness error
[ ] pkix-path documents that it cannot parse pre-1970 UTCTime, that RFC 5280 section 4.1.2.5.1 permits 1950-2049, and that the failure is fail-closed

## Withdrawn from this bead

The 8-chain drift and the red gate are now PKIX-ygs2. The pyca DSA-parameter-inheritance oracle error goes there too -- it is the same class of problem, an oracle limitation surfacing as a harness error.","priority":3,"title":"pkix-path cannot parse pre-1970 UTCTime (der 0.8.3 limitation, fail-closed)"}
